summary: This bill designates the Department of Veterans Affairs multispecialty clinic at 1263 Cobb Parkway NW in Marietta, Georgia, as the Colonel Michael H. Boyce Department of Veterans Affairs Multispecialty Clinic and requires all references to it to use that name.

scores.thoughts: The bill solely renames an existing Department of Veterans Affairs multispecialty clinic in Marietta, Georgia, after Colonel Michael H. Boyce. It includes findings about his life and service but authorizes no new appropriations, expansions, or reductions in government spending. The facility already exists, so there is no fiscal impact.
The bill makes no mention of taxes, tax rates, deductions, or any tax policy. It is purely a naming measure for a VA clinic.

While the bill concerns a VA multispecialty clinic, which provides healthcare to veterans, it only renames the existing facility without altering coverage, funding, access, structure, or any healthcare policy. The findings praise the colonel's efforts in establishing the clinic, but the bill itself effects no change.
The bill has no reference to guns, firearms, regulations, or rights related to them.
No content related to immigration, borders, pathways, or protections.
No mention of abortion or reproductive rights.

The bill honors a retired Marine Corps colonel via naming a VA clinic, but VA operations are distinct from active military and defense spending. No provisions affect military budgets, procurement, or operations.
No environmental regulations, protections, or climate-related content.
VA clinics support veterans, potentially overlapping with safety nets, but the bill only renames an existing clinic without expanding, scaling back, or changing any benefits or programs.
No relation to education policy, schools, or funding.
No content on drugs, enforcement, or decriminalization.
No provisions on sentencing, policing, reform, or justice system.
